events.content: The whole page is one async component awaiting `getInventory()`, so with `cacheComponents: true` in next.config.ts, the entire page — including the static title — blocks on that dynamic data fetch before anything is sent to the browser. The fix is to move the data-dependent part into its own component wrapped in `Suspense`, so the shell (title) renders immediately and streams while inventory data loads.

events.content:
Build confirms `/product` now uses **Partial Prerender** — the shell (with the title) is prerendered as static HTML, and only the inventory data streams in dynamically. Previously the whole route was fully dynamic. Fixed: `app/product/page.tsx` now renders `

Premium Widget

` in the static shell, with the inventory-dependent markup split into a separate `Inventory` component wrapped in `Suspense`. The title ships immediately; stock/price stream in once `getInventory()` resolves.
